synopsis: The four-month validation window is feasible only if preparatory work, including simulation credibility, finishes before the prototype arrives in mid-2027; no standard guarantees that a first-time simulation organization can achieve it [f11340, f14526, f7594]. Sensor and prototype freeze dates set the critical path: the sensor choice should be locked by early 2027 because it gates sensor-specific models and data collection, while a later modality change costs time through reworking strata and samples [f11915, f1616, f2006, f7492]. Independent review can become another critical path: University of Pretoria verification reported 1.6 tests per week and an 18-week lead time in October 2025, supporting immediate booking and provision for at least one retest [f683, f5180, f5790]. Immature technology is the most consistently documented cause of schedule failure, but the prior three-to-four-year effort lacks a root-cause time breakdown, leaving requirements definition and field tuning as possible bottlenecks rather than test count [f204, f273, f10854, f10859]. Planning should locate integration and pre-correlation buffers, distinguish uncertainty from contingency rather than add 20% everywhere, and expose long-lead external dependencies; notified-body and heavy-machine facility access times remain unresolved [f10244, f9650, f9641, f10245, f801, f5120].
